title: Vulvar Surgery Pudendal Nerve Block
official: Pudendal Blocks for Pain Control in Oncologic Vulvar Surgery: A Randomized Control Trial
summary:
The purpose of this research is to determine if a pudendal nerve block will help decrease postoperative pain after vulvar surgery.

The main questions answered:

* Does pudendal nerve block decrease post-operative pain?
* Does pudendal nerve block decrease post-operative opioid use?

Researchers will compare a pudendal block to no pudendal block to see whether there is a difference to patients.

Participants will:

* Either receive or not receive a pudendal block during vulvar surgery
* Answer questions about post-operative pain up to post-operative day 1
* Have surgical and clinical variables collected to understand the association between surgery, pudendal nerve block, and post-operative pain
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women 18 years of age or older who are undergoing vulvar surgery (wide local excision, radical vulvectomy, or simple vulvectomy) with gynecologic oncology
* Women who are undergoing concurrent lymph node evaluation can be included
* Women who are undergoing concomitant procedure with their vulvar surgery to include: biopsy, laser ablation or cavitational ultrasonic surgical aspiration (CUSA)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Women who have substance abuse history and currently on opioid maintenance therapy, or who continue to abuse opioids
* Women who are only having a vulvar biopsy, laser ablation, or cavitational ultrasonic surgical aspiration (CUSA) without a vulvar surgery
* Women with current diagnosis of chronic pelvic pain
